atoms.text: This guide configures the fictional service VaultSync Replicator to copy new objects from the S3 bucket app-uploads-primary to the S3 bucket app-uploads-dr for disaster recovery. Both buckets and the IAM role vaultsync-replication-role belong to account 111111111111. Create the role with a trust policy that allows the VaultSync service to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication and s3:ListBucket on app-uploads-primary, and s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on app-uploads-dr/*. Because the role and the destination bucket are in the same account, this identity-based policy is the only place the grant is made. Leave the bucket policy on app-uploads-dr unchanged. Enable versioning on both buckets, then create a replication rule for the prefix uploads/ that references the role's ARN. Upload a test object under uploads/ and confirm that its replication status moves from PENDING to COMPLETED.

This guide configures the fictional service VaultSync Replicator to copy new objects from the S3 bucket app-uploads-primary in account 111111111111 to the S3 bucket app-uploads-dr, which is owned by account 222222222222. The IAM role vaultsync-replication-role is in account 111111111111. Create the role with a trust policy that allows the VaultSync service to assume it, and attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication and s3:ListBucket on app-uploads-primary. The owner of account 222222222222 then adds a statement to the bucket policy of app-uploads-dr. That statement names arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/vaultsync-replication-role as the principal and allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on app-uploads-dr/*. Because the destination bucket is in a different account, this bucket policy statement carries the grant for writes to the destination. Enable versioning on both buckets, then create a replication rule for the prefix uploads/ that references the role's ARN. Upload a test object under uploads/ and confirm that its replication status moves from PENDING to COMPLETED.

This guide gives a nightly database backup job permission to write dump files to the S3 bucket db-dumps-nightly. The job is run by the fictional tool SnapshotShipper under the IAM role db-backup-uploader. The role and the bucket are both in account 111111111111. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on db-dumps-nightly, with the object resource limited to pg/daily/*. Because both resources are in the same account, the identity-based policy is the only grant required and the bucket policy is not changed. Configure SnapshotShipper to upload each compressed dump as a multipart upload using 64 MiB parts. Set a lifecycle rule on the bucket to expire objects under pg/daily/ after 35 days. Run the job once manually and verify that a file named with the current date appears under pg/daily/.

This guide gives a nightly database backup job permission to write dump files to the S3 bucket db-dumps-nightly. The job is run by the fictional tool SnapshotShipper under the IAM role db-backup-uploader in account 111111111111, while the bucket is owned by account 222222222222. The owner of account 222222222222 adds a statement to the bucket policy of db-dumps-nightly. That statement names arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/db-backup-uploader as the principal and allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads, with the object resource limited to pg/daily/*. Because the bucket is in a different account, the bucket policy statement is what grants the access across the account boundary. Configure SnapshotShipper to upload each compressed dump as a multipart upload using 64 MiB parts. Set a lifecycle rule on the bucket to expire objects under pg/daily/ after 35 days. Run the job once manually and verify that a file named with the current date appears under pg/daily/.

This guide lets a restore workflow read archived backups from the S3 bucket backup-archive-main. The workflow is run by the fictional service RestoreRelay under the IAM role restore-runner. The role and the bucket are in account 111111111111. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on backup-archive-main/restore-sets/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with an s3:prefix condition of restore-sets/. The identity-based policy is the sole grant in this configuration, and the bucket policy of backup-archive-main is not modified. In RestoreRelay, set the source location to s3://backup-archive-main/restore-sets/ and select the target volume. The workflow only reads from the bucket and writes restored data to the target volume. Start a test restore of a small set and confirm that the object count in the job report matches the listing.

This guide lets a restore workflow read archived backups from the S3 bucket backup-archive-main. The owner of account 222222222222 adds a statement to the bucket policy of backup-archive-main that names arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/restore-runner as the principal. The statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on backup-archive-main/restore-sets/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with an s3:prefix condition of restore-sets/. This bucket policy statement is the grant, because the bucket is in a different account from the role. In RestoreRelay, set the source location to s3://backup-archive-main/restore-sets/ and select the target volume. The workflow only reads from the bucket and writes restored data to the target volume. Start a test restore of a small set and confirm that the object count in the job report matches the listing.

This guide configures retention-locked replication of financial ledger exports into the S3 bucket ledger-vault-copy for long-term recovery. The fictional service LedgerMirror copies objects from ledger-exports under the IAM role ledgermirror-role. The source bucket, the destination bucket and the role are all in account 111111111111. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication and s3:GetObjectRetention on ledger-exports/*, and s3:ReplicateObject and s3:PutObjectRetention on ledger-vault-copy/*. The grant is made only in this identity-based policy, and the bucket policy of ledger-vault-copy remains unchanged. Enable versioning and Object Lock on the destination bucket with a default retention of 7 years in compliance mode. Create a LedgerMirror rule that replicates the prefix monthly/ using the role. After the next export, check that the replica carries the same retain-until date as the source object.

This guide configures retention-locked replication of financial ledger exports into the S3 bucket ledger-vault-copy for long-term recovery. The fictional service LedgerMirror copies objects from ledger-exports in account 111111111111 under the IAM role ledgermirror-role, while ledger-vault-copy is owned by account 222222222222. The role has an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication and s3:GetObjectRetention on ledger-exports/*. The owner of account 222222222222 adds a bucket policy statement to ledger-vault-copy that names arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/ledgermirror-role as the principal and allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:PutObjectRetention on ledger-vault-copy/*. That statement is the grant for the destination, since the bucket is in a different account. Enable versioning and Object Lock on the destination bucket with a default retention of 7 years in compliance mode. Create a LedgerMirror rule that replicates the prefix monthly/ using the role. After the next export, check that the replica carries the same retain-until date as the source object.

This guide allows a log forwarding agent to deposit compressed audit log archives into the S3 bucket audit-logs-archive. The agent is the fictional tool TrailBundler, which runs under the IAM role trailbundler-writer. The role and the bucket are in account 111111111111. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows only s3:PutObject on audit-logs-archive/logs/*, with a condition requiring the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal AES256. No other grant is needed, and the bucket policy is left as it is. Configure TrailBundler to write one gzip file per hour using the key pattern logs/YYYY/MM/DD/HH.log.gz. The role has no permission to list, read or delete objects, so a failed upload can only be diagnosed from the agent's local log. Upload a sample file and confirm it is stored with the expected encryption setting.

The agent is the fictional tool TrailBundler, which runs under the IAM role trailbundler-writer in account 111111111111, and the bucket is owned by account 222222222222. The owner of account 222222222222 adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/trailbundler-writer as the principal. The statement allows only s3:PutObject on audit-logs-archive/logs/*, with a condition requiring the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal AES256. This statement carries the grant because the bucket is in a different account. Configure TrailBundler to write one gzip file per hour using the key pattern logs/YYYY/MM/DD/HH.log.gz. Upload a sample file and confirm it is stored with the expected encryption setting.

This guide configures a scheduled mirror job that keeps the S3 bucket media-standby in step with media-origin. The job is run by the fictional service MirrorPulse under the IAM role mirrorpulse-sync. Both buckets and the role are in account 111111111111. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on media-origin, and s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject and s3:ListBucket on media-standby. Because everything is in one account, this identity-based policy is the only place access is granted, and neither bucket policy is changed. Set the MirrorPulse schedule to run every 30 minutes and compare objects by size and ETag. Enable the delete-stale option so that objects removed from media-origin are also removed from media-standby. Run a dry-run first and review the planned copy and delete counts before enabling the schedule.

This guide configures a scheduled mirror job that keeps the S3 bucket media-standby in step with media-origin. The job is run by the fictional service MirrorPulse under the IAM role mirrorpulse-sync in account 111111111111, which also owns media-origin. The bucket media-standby is owned by account 222222222222. The role's identity-based policy allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on media-origin. The owner of account 222222222222 adds a statement to the bucket policy of media-standby that names arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/mirrorpulse-sync as the principal and allows s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject and s3:ListBucket. This bucket policy statement carries the grant for the standby side. Set the MirrorPulse schedule to run every 30 minutes and compare objects by size and ETag. Enable the delete-stale option so that objects removed from media-origin are also removed from media-standby. Run a dry-run first and review the planned copy and delete counts before enabling the schedule.

This guide grants an IAM user, backup-agent-user, access to the S3 bucket fs-backup-store for incremental file server backups. The user's access keys are used by the fictional agent FileTrove on server fs01. The user and the bucket are in account 111111111111. Attach an identity-based policy to the user that allows s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on fs-backup-store/fs01/chunks/* and fs-backup-store/fs01/manifests/*, plus s3:ListBucket with an s3:prefix condition of fs01/. This identity-based policy is the only grant, and the bucket policy is not edited. Store the access keys in the agent's credential file with file mode 600. FileTrove uploads changed data blocks as chunks and writes a manifest after each run. It reads the previous manifest to determine which blocks changed. Run a full backup followed by an incremental one and confirm that the second run uploads only the changed chunks.

The statement allows s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on fs-backup-store/fs01/chunks/* and fs-backup-store/fs01/manifests/*, plus s3:ListBucket with an s3:prefix condition of fs01/. This bucket policy statement is the grant, since the bucket is in a different account. Store the access keys in the agent's credential file with file mode 600. FileTrove uploads changed data blocks as chunks and writes a manifest after each run. It reads the previous manifest to determine which blocks changed. Run a full backup followed by an incremental one and confirm that the second run uploads only the changed chunks.

This guide gives a backup integrity verifier access to the S3 bucket backup-vault-eu. The verifier is the fictional service ChecksumWarden, which runs under the IAM role checksumwarden-runner. The role and the bucket are in account 111111111111. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectAttributes on backup-vault-eu/sets/*, s3:ListBucket on the bucket, and s3:PutObject on backup-vault-eu/reports/*. This identity-based policy is the only grant, and the bucket policy remains unchanged. Configure ChecksumWarden to read each object under sets/ weekly and compare its SHA-256 checksum with the value in the backup catalog. It writes one JSON report per run to reports/ and never modifies objects under sets/. Trigger a manual run and confirm that a report appears with a mismatch count of zero.
